method: HOUSECARL_SKILL_AUTHORING.md §6.5 manual validation (run_loop.py uses select(), broken on Windows per §6.4). Empirical step = independent fan-out of 20 fresh-context Sonnet agents, one per query, each shown a neutral menu of 9 skill descriptions (spid-authoring among realistic siblings, NOT flagged as under-test) + one query, asked which ONE skill to load (or none) + reasoning. Anonymized per feedback_skill_trigger_eval_fanout (skill not named; question framed as routing, not 'would you load this'); each agent told to judge ONLY the provided menu and ignore its own environment skills (spid-authoring is auto-discoverable on disk, so this neutralizes the self-contamination trap). Verdicts adjudicated from each agent's REASONING + pick. Menu order (SPID placed at C, not first, to blunt primacy bias): A=SkyPatcher edit-record-fields, B=KID keywords-to-items, C=SPID distribute-to-NPCs [under test], D=CID items-to-containers, E=mutagen-reference record-schema, F=crash-diagnostics, G=conflict-resolution, H=papyrus-reference, I=modding-basics install/CK/concepts. Run 2026-06-02.

result.notes: All 10 should-trigger picked C (SPID), including the 3 implicit cases that never say 'SPID' (q4 power+Unique trait, q6 level/skill filter 'no esp', q7 item+count 'no plugin') and the AI-package case (q9). All 10 should-not correctly routed elsewhere — incl. the three hardest near-misses: q18 ('install SPID in MO2'→I) and q19 ('what is SPID, I'm new'→I) both name SPID but are not authoring; q20 ('enchant all iron swords at runtime'→A) is runtime+apply-to-many but targets ITEMS not NPCs. Agents consistently discriminated on SPID's defining axis (target = NPCs vs items=KID vs containers=CID vs record-fields=SkyPatcher), which matches the SKILL.md scope boundary. Every manual_predicted_trigger matched the measured verdict.
result.peer_review: Author prediction + 20 independent fresh-context Sonnet agents (exceeds §6.5's 'one peer reviewer checks 3 random'). Aaron may spot-check any query.
result.carry_forward: KI-S5-V1X-1: re-run on the next release that ships a Windows-compatible eval runner (run_loop.py select() fix), per §6.4.
